title: Scout G-S3 (daemon stage stamps, automatic fix rounds, review triggers): crash windows between stamp and action, what an automatic fix task needs and already exists, and where semantic review triggers and commit-bound approval would go
spec:
Goal T-0260 has three daemon items. Inventory with path:line for each:
1. Stage stamps: orchestrator/daemon.py stamp() and every stage that stamps then acts (dispatched_at, spec_review_at, gated_at, review spawn, merged_at, review_held_at). For each: what happens if the process dies between the stamp and the action (is the stage skipped forever, retried, or reconciled by reconcile()/requeue of dead processes/already_merged()); which of these already reconcile against git or process state. Rank the windows by likelihood and damage. Propose the smallest state model (claimed/started/completed with a lease and reconciliation) that fits stamp() as it is.
2. Automatic fix rounds: what the daemon knows when a task is held (hold_reason, resume_hint.failures from tests-green, review comments with path/line/severity, acceptance, scope, branch and commit) and which of it a Python-generated fix-task spec could use without a model; the existing pieces (constraints.fix_round_for, spawn.base_for, planner_runs held decision point, fit_result, fix-delta.md prompt); where merged_into reconciliation of the original task would hook after a fix round merges (merge_reviewed, merge.py). Define the boundary: routine (gate red with failing test ids or review request_changes with concrete path/line comments, scope unchanged) versus escalate (spec_review request_changes, conflicts, missing files outside scope, no concrete failure).
3. Review triggers and approval binding: daemon.changed_paths and the security_paths policy (where the glob match happens); what it would take to also match diff content or paths for authorization behaviour, migrations, public interfaces (module __all__, MCP tool signatures, CLI args), dependency files (pyproject, uv.lock, Dockerfile); how a review verdict is stored (review_verdict on the review task and on src, no commit sha) and what merge.merge does after approval (rebase, tests) so a rebase with real changes still merges under the old approval; where to record the reviewed commit and compare after rebase.
Report three sections with path:line, a ranked risk table for section 1, the routine/escalate rule for section 2, the trigger list and binding point for section 3. Under 1,500 tokens, confidence per finding.
acceptance: section 1 lists each stamp-then-act window with its recovery status and a ranked risk table
section 2 states the routine versus escalate rule and names the existing pieces to reuse
section 3 names the match point for semantic triggers and where approval would be bound to a commit
result under 1,500 tokens with a confidence per finding

findings.claim: stamp() claims a pipeline stage under bus.locked() before daemon.py acts, so a crash between stamp and action leaves the task wedged, not skipped or auto-retried (no lease/TTL)

dispatched_at (dispatch): crash after stamp before executor.start leaves task queued+stamped forever; only reconciled if bus status flips to running then pid dies (tick's requeue at daemon.py:212-214), not by the dispatch stamp itself

spec_review_at: crash after stamp before bus.create_task/spawn_async leaves task stuck queued with no spec_review task ever created; nothing reconciles this (dispatch() skips re-creating since stamp already set)

gated_at: stamp happens after tests-green already ran and after the merge-vs-review branch decision starts; crash inside the try block leaves task done+gated with no merge/review ever spawned, unrecovered except by hold_failed on raised exceptions

merged_at (merge_reviewed, approve path): stamped before merge.merge() runs; crash mid-merge leaves review done+stamped with src never merged and merged_into unset, and no retry path since the stamp blocks future ticks

already_merged() partially reconciles the merged_at/dispatched gap: it detects a task's branch already an ancestor of goal/<parent> via merge-base --is-ancestor even when merged_into is unset, self-healing fix-round merges

review_held_at and spec_review_held_at stamps are terminal by design (status set to held in the same stamp call), intentionally not auto-recovered — comments say the Planner must write the fix-round spec

Ranked risk (damage x likelihood): 1) merged_at crash mid-merge.merge (silent lost merge, no auto-retry) 2) gated_at crash before review/merge spawn (done task orphaned) 3) spec_review_at crash before task creation (queued task orphaned) 4) dispatched_at crash before executor.start (recovered within 60s by tick's dead-pid requeue, lowest damage)

Smallest fitting state model: keep stamp()'s single bus_lock claim but split each pipeline.<stage>_at into claimed_at/completed_at pair with a lease timestamp; tick() sweeps stages where claimed_at is set, completed_at is unset, and lease expired, re-running the action (idempotent by design: create_task calls already dedupe via bus.read role checks at daemon.py:136, merge.merge is safe to re-call since it checks already_merged first)

On held tasks the daemon/bus already carries hold_reason and resume_hint (e.g. {failures:...} from tests-green, {conflicts,hunks} from rebase) that a Python fix-spec generator could reuse without a model call

No constraints.fix_round_for, spawn.base_for-driven fix-round spec builder, or automatic fix-task spec generation exists in this worktree's orchestrator/*.py — fix rounds are currently manual: Planner calls codex_reply with a delta text against fix-delta.md (round {{n}}/5, failing_tests, assertion_lines), and merge_reviewed()/dispatch() explicitly hold and defer to the Planner instead of writing a spec
gotchas.md records that fix rounds leave the original task without merged_into, which is exactly what already_merged() at daemon.py:59-81 was built to reconcile before gate/review re-run

open_questions: Does the security_paths/changed_paths feature from bus:T-0221-T-0225 exist on a different branch (e.g. goal/T-0221) not yet merged to this worktree's base — worth checking main or that goal branch directly
Is there a separate module (e.g. constraints.py) for fix_round_for/spawn.base_for referenced in the task prompt that lives outside orchestrator/ — not found in this worktree
suggested_next: Diff this worktree's base against goal/T-0221..T-0225 branches to locate the security_paths implementation before designing section 3's extension
Confirm with Planner whether fix-round automation (section 2) is intentionally manual-only per merge_reviewed()'s comment, or whether a constraints.py module was planned but not yet written
